TryModifyPowerAmountReceived.maps_to: cmds.py:299-306, a hand-written branch inside PowerCmd.apply -- ArtifactPower itself declares no hook (powers.py:315-325)
TryModifyPowerAmountReceived.issue: The interception is reimplemented outside the hook system entirely, and the debuff test is the wrong one. C# (ArtifactPower.cs:17-36) is a TryModifyPowerAmountReceived listener whose three guards are `target != Owner`, `canonicalPower.GetTypeForAmount(amount) != Debuff`, and `!canonicalPower.IsVisible`; cmds.py:299 instead tests the applied class's static `power_cls.power_type == PowerType.DEBUFF`. That is audit/records/seam/power_cmd.json's gap G1 and its guard G3 (Artifact is not a modify_power_amount listener at all); per binding rule 3 this entry carries the identical verdict and is cross-referenced rather than re-argued -- DORMANT in both directions, trigger = porting Malaise.cs:39 or Resonance.cs:33. Recorded here because it is THIS unit's only real behaviour and a reader of artifact.json must not be left thinking the port is hook-shaped.

AfterModifyingPowerAmountReceived.issue: ADJUDICATION 2026-07-30 (round 11, batch power-5) -- this entry was the blocking tie-break between damage_pipeline/G2 (recorded 'live', citing this exact PowerAmountReceived edge via power_cmd/G4's 'Unsettling Lamp seam') and this batch's assignment to determine reachability by execution. SETTLED: DORMANT. The stack-consumption event is hand-inlined -- C# consumes the stack via `PowerCmd.Decrement(this)` from AfterModifyingPowerAmountReceived (ArtifactPower.cs:38-41), which re-enters the FULL PowerCmd.ModifyAmount pipeline (PowerCmd.cs:215-271) on the ArtifactPower instance itself: `await Hook.BeforePowerAmountChanged(combatState, power=Artifact, offset=-1, owner, applier=null, cardSource=null)` (:227), `Hook.ModifyPowerAmountGiven` skipped (applier is null, :230 guard fails), `Hook.ModifyPowerAmountReceived(combatState, canonicalPower=Artifact, owner, -1, giver=null, ...)` (:234). The sim's cmds.py:559-565 inline block runs none of this. EXHAUSTIVE ENUMERATION of every C# override of the three hooks fired (`grep -rln 'override.*BeforePowerAmountChanged\|override.*ModifyPowerAmountGiven\|override.*ModifyPowerAmountReceived' src/Core/Models/Powers/ src/Core/Models/Relics/`): BeforePowerAmountChanged -> VoidFormPower (unported: `grep -rn 'class VoidFormPower' sts2_rl/` returns nothing), UnsettlingLamp; ModifyPowerAmountGiven(Additive/Multiplicative) -> SneckoSkull, UnsettlingLamp (never invoked at all on this call: applier is always null, PowerCmd.cs:230's guard short-circuits before either listener is reached); TryModifyPowerAmountReceived -> ArtifactPower (self, since IterateCombatHookListeners walks every AbstractModel in combat including the power being modified), RuinedHelmet, MockRevivePower (test mock under Powers/Mocks/, not decompiled content). EVERY one of these bails UNCONDITIONALLY for this exact call shape, independent of any game state: UnsettlingLamp.BeforePowerAmountChanged returns immediately on `cardSource == null` (UnsettlingLamp.cs:81) and cardSource is always null on this call (PowerCmd.Decrement passes null,null); VoidFormPower.BeforePowerAmountChanged returns immediately on `power != this` (VoidFormPower.cs:30) and power is the Artifact instance, never a VoidFormPower instance; ArtifactPower's own TryModifyPowerAmountReceived (self-listen) returns false because `canonicalPower.GetTypeForAmount(amount) != PowerType.Debuff` is true -- ArtifactPower does not override AllowNegative (default false, ArtifactPower.cs has no such override) and Type=Buff, so GetTypeForAmount(-1) returns Buff per PowerModel.cs:460-470's own branching (neither the Counter-AllowNegative branch nor the Debuff-flip branch applies); RuinedHelmet.TryModifyPowerAmountReceived returns false on `!(canonicalPower is StrengthPower)` (RuinedHelmet.cs:35) and canonicalPower is ArtifactPower, never StrengthPower. Consequently AfterModifyingPowerAmountGiven never fires (Given chain never ran) and AfterModifyingPowerAmountReceived's own `receivedModifiers` list is empty (no TryModifyPowerAmountReceived call returned true), so it iterates zero listeners. CROSS-VERIFIED on the sim side by EXECUTION (`.superpowers/sdd/unlabelled/probes/power-5-artifact-adjudication.py`): the sim's only two `modify_power_amount` listeners (UnsettlingLamp, RuinedHelmet -- `grep -rn 'def modify_power_amount' sts2_rl/` finds exactly the dispatcher plus these two) were called with the exact shape Artifact's self-decrement would produce if wired (`power_cls=ArtifactPower, amount=-1, applier=None`), with Lamp pre-armed maximally favorably (`_in_flight` set, not yet finished) and Helmet pre-armed maximally favorably (`_used=False`): `modify_power_amount(ArtifactPower, player, -1, None) -> -1` (unchanged), Lamp's `_triggering` stayed `None`, Helmet's `_used` stayed `False` -- both relics are inert by construction (Lamp checks `amount <= 0` first and always bails on a decrement; Helmet checks `power_cls is StrengthPower`, which ArtifactPower can never satisfy). Both enumerations agree: no ported listener, in either codebase, can observe Artifact's own stack decrement through this pipeline, for structural reasons that hold under ANY game state, not merely current-content absence. THEREFORE: this settles damage_pipeline/G2's inherited 'live' edge (via power_cmd/G4's PowerAmountReceived citation) as FALSE -- reported to the controller for damage_pipeline.json, not edited here (out of this batch's ownership). The mechanism itself remains a real, unfixed divergence (the sim still does not run the pipeline; a future third `modify_power_amount` listener whose domain includes negative/Artifact-typed amounts, or a future `before_power_amount_changed` sim hook with a non-null-cardSource-tolerant listener, would need this fixed) -- hence `gap` with `live: false`, not `faithful`.

The sim has no IsVisible concept. Genuinely inert rather than merely untriggered: PowerModel.IsVisible (src/Core/Models/PowerModel.cs:150-160 -- the file sits directly under Models/, NOT under Models/Powers/) returns IsVisibleInternal, the overridable virtual at PowerModel.cs:167, for a self-or-enemy target, and EXECUTED -- `py audit/tools/power_census.py visible` -- **0 of the 260 .cs files directly under src/Core/Models/Powers override IsVisibleInternal** (260 EXCLUDES the 16 files in Powers/Mocks/; 276 including them, and a recursive grep that does cover Mocks/ also returns 0), so it is provably always true for every power in the whole decompiled game, not just the ported ones. Same finding and same verdict as power_cmd note N1. PROMPT.md bug class 4 (visibility guards) is therefore CLEAR for this unit and for every other power unit. Third-file citations, not hashed here.
